focus: Transport-neutral CLI core over the existing 40 MCP tool handlers
noveltyJustification: First pass established the shared 40-tool definition array, transport-coupled dispatch, argv parsing hazard, separate entry requirement, and shutdown cleanup boundary.
keyQuestions: How can dispatchToolCall be made transport-neutral and shared by MCP and CLI while keeping argument errors as CLI results?
answeredQuestions: How can dispatchToolCall be made transport-neutral and shared by MCP and CLI while keeping argument errors as CLI results?

ruledOut.approach: Spawn the MCP stdio server for each CLI call
ruledOut.reason: Keeps CLI execution coupled to protocol framing and server lifecycle

ruledOut.approach: Maintain a separate CLI handler table
ruledOut.evidence: AI Systems/Media Editor/mcp server/src/server/create-server.ts:43-56, AI Systems/Media Editor/mcp server/src/server/all-tools.ts:57-98

findings: The server and proposed CLI can share the canonical 40-entry ALL_TOOLS array.
The dispatcher owns validation, placement, and result conversion but currently throws MCP protocol errors for invalid arguments.
A new CLI entry is required because importing src/index.ts immediately runs its MCP main.
Tool argv must never be passed to loadConfig because bare tokens become allowed roots.
CLI signal cleanup needs process cancellation and awaited temp cleanup beyond current per-call timeout handling.
